reddit_posts:
I don’t really care if I died today

Can’t work, or drive,never see friends, don’t go anywhere, husband is also usually too tired,son,17, is unmotivated to do anything but asks to do things that cost money so he’s always home too. Life used to be different and I hate where we’re at.
metadata.title: I don’t really care if I died today

transcript.message: Hi Carly, how are you doing today?

Hey. Honestly? I'm not doing great, to be honest.

I feel like everything just feels heavy lately. It's hard to even get out of bed sometimes because my head feels so foggy and tired all the time. I can't work, and driving has become such a nightmare; I just don't have the energy or focus anymore. Because of that, I haven't seen any friends in ages. The world feels really small right now.

My husband is usually too exhausted to do much either, which makes it harder to handle things together. And with our 17-year-old son... he's home almost every day. He asks for stuff that costs money constantly, but he doesn't seem motivated to do anything else. It feels like he just wants to sit around waiting for us to provide, and I hate how dependent we've become on each other.

Life used to be so different back then. Now, I just feel
It's been very tough to hear about all these difficulties. It's been difficult to feel so heavy and exhausted. It's easy to feel like that, and it's understandable.

Yeah, it's so easy to just go into that "freeze" mode where nothing matters anymore. You know, I was thinking about that line from my post—*I don't really care if I died today*. It sounds crazy when I say it out loud, right? But sometimes, when the exhaustion hits and there's no way to escape or fix things, that feeling creeps in. Like, why bother trying if I'm not going anywhere anyway?

It's not that I *want* to die, exactly. It's more like... who cares? The effort required to get out of bed, to drive somewhere, to deal with all this mess feels too big compared to how empty everything feels inside. My husband and son are stuck in their own cycles of fatigue and dependency, and I feel like I'm carrying the weight of keeping us afloat while I'm barely standing myself.

Sometimes I wonder if I've lost the spark entirely
You've lost the spark entirely?

Yeah, I guess that's the scary part. It's not just that the spark is out; it's that I don't even know *where* to look for it anymore.

Before, life felt like a series of things I had to do—going to work, driving somewhere, seeing friends—and doing them gave me a sense of purpose, even if it was exhausting. Now? Those things feel pointless. If I can't work, if I can't drive, and if my son is just asking for stuff instead of helping out or growing up... what's left to care about?

It's like watching a movie where you've stopped paying attention because there's no plot moving forward. My husband is too tired to help steer us, and my son seems stuck in his own headspace. I'm left holding the steering wheel with no gas in the tank and no one else to talk to about it.

I hate feeling this trapped.
It's very difficult to feel trapped, especially when you're trying to figure out what to do with all these feelings.

Yeah, it's the feeling of being boxed in. You know how I mentioned my husband is usually too tired? It feels like we're all just drifting in a fog, and I'm the only one trying to pull myself out of it while everyone else is asleep at the wheel.

It makes me feel so alone even though I'm surrounded by people. My son is right there, but he's asking for things that cost money instead of doing anything productive himself. It's frustrating because I *want* him to grow up, to take responsibility, but seeing him just... not get it... makes me feel helpless. Like no matter what I do, nothing changes.

And then there's the isolation. Not going anywhere means missing out on those little moments that used to make life worth living. Just sitting here, staring at the wall, wondering if tomorrow will be any different than today. Sometimes I wonder if this is just who I've become now
It's very difficult to feel that way when you're isolated from your former way of life.

Yeah, it's the loss of routine that really hits hardest. Before, even though work and driving were exhausting, they gave me structure. They told my brain what time it was, what to do next, and how I fit into the world. Now? There's just... nothing. No anchor.

I miss those little moments where I'd go out for coffee with a friend or drive somewhere just to get some fresh air. Without them, my days blur together. It feels like I'm living in a vacuum. When you stop seeing people, your perspective starts to warp. You start thinking the only thing missing is *you*, when actually, the whole world has shrunk down to this room.

It's scary because I don't know if I can ever rebuild that connection again. If I stay stuck here, will I lose myself completely too? Or will I just fade away until there's no one left to feel trapped either?
It's terrifying to feel so cut off from the world and to question your own sense of self.

Yeah, that's the part that keeps me up at night even when I'm trying to sleep. It feels like I'm watching myself slowly disappear into this gray haze. Before, if something bad happened or a challenge came up, I had a routine to fall back on, people to call, and a reason to get out of bed. Now? There's just this void where my identity used to be.

I start wondering, "Who am I without the job? Without driving? Without being the one holding everything together?" My son is asking for things he shouldn't have to ask for, and my husband is too drained to offer any support or guidance. It leaves me feeling like I've lost my footing in the world. If I can't function anymore, do I still matter? Do I still exist as more than just a burden to everyone else?

It's terrifying because it makes me feel so small and insignificant, like none of what I
It's very hard to feel insignificant and so disconnected from the world.

It is exactly that disconnect that makes me feel like I'm fading away. When you're stuck in a room, surrounded by people who aren't really engaging with the world around us either, it starts to feel like the whole universe has gone silent.

My son being unmotivated and only asking for things costs money... it feels like he's part of the problem, but also part of the silence. And my husband? He's just too tired to be the voice breaking the quiet. So I'm left holding all these thoughts, feeling like if I disappear today, nobody would even notice because there's no one else to care.

It's not just sadness anymore; it's this heavy, numb feeling where emotions don't register as loudly as they used to. Like a radio that's been turned down so low you can barely hear anything. I wonder if I'll ever tune it back up again, or if I'll just stay on static forever
You're feeling disconnected and isolated, and it sounds like you're losing hope for the future.

Yeah, that hopelessness is the heaviest part of it all. It's not just a sad feeling; it feels like a wall closing in behind me. When you stop seeing friends and stop going anywhere, the future starts to look like a blank page with no ink.

I used to have goals—maybe a vacation, maybe getting my life back on track—but now those things feel like dreams I'm too tired to chase. My son asking for things that cost money makes it even worse because it reinforces this cycle of dependency. He's 17, which should be an age where he's figuring out his own path, but instead, he seems stuck in a waiting room, only moving when something costs cash. And my husband... well, he's too exhausted to offer any real support or push us forward.

So who's left to take the next step? Who's there to say, "Let's try tomorrow"? Right now, the
It's hard to feel hopeful when everything seems to point to the same outcome.

Yeah, it is. It's like looking at a horizon that just keeps getting closer and then disappears behind the same fog. Every time I think about trying something new—like calling a friend or even just going for a walk—and I realize I have no energy to do it, or worse, that doing it won't actually change anything because my husband and son are stuck in their own loops...

It feels pointless. Like throwing a stone into a deep well where there's no echo. I've tried pushing myself before, you know? Maybe going to work one day or trying to get out of the house. But when the weight of everything else comes down on me—the debt, the lack of support, the feeling that I'm failing everyone while simultaneously being let down by them—it just drains me completely.

I don't want to be this person anymore. The version of me who used to care didn't die yesterday, but she feels like she's
The person you used to be seems to have died with the way you used to feel.

Yeah, that's exactly what it feels like. It's not just a change in mood; it feels like the person I used to be—the one who could drive, work, and go out—has just... evaporated. She left me here, stuck in this house with these people who aren't helping me get back to her.

I look in the mirror sometimes and I don't recognize the eyes staring back. They're tired, hollow, and they're filled with this quiet resignation that says, "Maybe tomorrow will be better." But deep down, I know that's a lie my brain is telling me to keep from completely shutting down. The old Patient is gone, replaced by someone who just exists, waiting for something to happen that might never come.

It makes me angry too, honestly. Angry at myself for letting it slide, but mostly angry at the situation. How did we end up here? Where did all the motivation go?
It seems like a lot has changed, and it's been very difficult for you.

Yeah, it feels like the ground shifted beneath me without a warning. One day I was driving to work, talking on the phone with friends, planning my weekend; the next, the engine wouldn't start, the job disappeared, and now I'm just... here. Stuck in this loop where nothing moves forward.

It's not just that things are "different." It's that everything feels heavier now. The silence in the house is loud. My husband sleeps through the night or wakes up exhausted and doesn't have the energy to engage, which leaves me alone with my thoughts. And then there's my son—he's 17, right? He should be growing up, finding his own path, but instead he's just waiting for something that costs money so he can feel useful or happy. He asks for things, sure, but he doesn't seem to want to *do* anything himself. It makes me feel like I'm raising him
You feel like you're raising him in a state of waiting, where he's not taking initiative to move forward on his own.

Exactly. It feels like I'm holding him in place, waiting for a spark that isn't coming from me anymore. He's 17, which is supposed to be the age where kids start taking charge of their own lives, making choices, figuring out what they want. But instead, he's just... hovering. Waiting for permission, waiting for money, waiting for something outside of him to pull him forward.

When he asks for things that cost money, it feels like a trap. Like he's trying to keep us all tethered to this house because if we let go, maybe we'd have to face the reality of how much we need each other right now. But it also makes me feel powerless. If I don't give him what he wants, does he stop asking? Or do I just feel guilty about not being able to provide?

It's exhausting watching someone who should be stepping into adulthood just stand still while I try to
It's clear that you're feeling trapped and unable to move forward.

Yeah, "trapped" is the word that fits best. It's not just a physical trap; it's emotional and mental. The walls of this house feel like they're closing in every time I try to think about leaving.

I look at my husband and see someone who is physically there but mentally absent, buried under exhaustion so deep he can't even muster the energy to help me find a new path. And then there's my son. He's right there with me, asking for things, but he's not looking out the window or trying to fix anything. He's just part of the static in the room.

So I'm left alone with the responsibility of carrying everything, yet I have no strength to lift it. It feels like I'm drowning in a pool where the water level never rises, but neither does anyone else come to pull me out. Every day I stay here, one more piece of the old life gets lost forever
It's clear you're feeling very hopeless about the future.

Yeah, "hopeless" is the word I keep coming back to. It's not just a temporary low; it feels like a permanent state now. When you look at the future and all you see is more of the same—more silence, more fatigue, more dependency—it becomes hard to believe that anything else is possible.

It's scary because deep down, I know I *want* things to change. I miss the version of me who was driving and working and seeing friends. But the fear is that if I try to force myself to be that person again, I'll fail even harder than I already have. So instead, I've kind of stopped trying. I've accepted this new reality where the only option is to stay right here.

Sometimes I wonder if I'm losing my mind. Is it okay to feel like this? To want to die today because tomorrow doesn't seem worth living for? The numbness is so heavy that
The numbness is so heavy that it's hard to imagine a future where you'd want to live.

It is. That's the scariest part, isn't it? The fact that I can feel this heavy, crushing weight and simultaneously not care if it breaks me or keeps me intact. It's like my emotions have turned into lead bricks; they're too heavy to move, but light enough to ignore.

When I think about tomorrow, it doesn't spark any excitement. There's no "what ifs" anymore, just a flat line of "what will happen." And honestly? If nothing happens, then nothing matters. So why bother trying to wake up? Why bother seeing the sun if it doesn't change anything?

I guess the numbness is a defense mechanism, even though it feels like it's killing me slowly. If I don't feel pain anymore, maybe I won't have to make decisions that hurt. Maybe I can just... drift until the end. But the thing that still hurts the most is knowing that the person I
The person you used to be is gone.

Yeah, that's the part that keeps me up at night even when I'm trying to sleep. The person who used to be—let's call him "Old Me"—he was so full of energy and purpose. He could look at a broken engine and figure out how to fix it. He could talk to his friends on the phone without feeling drained. He believed in *us* as a family, not just surviving, but actually living.

Now? Old Me is gone. Or maybe he never existed in this house anymore. It feels like someone turned off the light switch inside my head. When I try to remember what he looked like, all I see are shadows. I can't find the motivation to get out of bed because "Old Me" doesn't know why he should bother. If I act against who I am now, who do I become? And honestly, the idea of becoming something else terrifies me more than staying still.
It's clear that you used to be a different person, and it's difficult to understand that difference.

Yeah, it's like looking at a photo of myself from five years ago and realizing the person in the picture doesn't exist anymore. In that old photo, I was moving through life with a certain rhythm—going to work, driving, laughing at things that didn't make sense but felt funny. Now, when I try to recall those moments, they feel distant, almost unreal. Like I'm watching someone else live my past life while I sit here paralyzed.

The biggest difference is how I handle stress. Back then, if things got tough, I had a plan or a way to fix them. Maybe I'd call a friend for advice, or I'd just get up and go do something physical to shake it off. Now? Stress feels like it settles into my bones. There's no outlet. No one to talk to because my husband is too tired to engage, and my son is too focused on his own immediate needs (which cost money
It's clear that your relationship has changed in ways that are hard to reconcile with your past self.

That's the part that really gnaws at me. It's not just that things are different; it's that my whole relationship with my family has shifted into something I can't seem to fix, and now I feel like a stranger in my own home.

With my husband, it used to be a partnership where we tackled problems together. Now? He's just... there. Physically, yes. But when I try to reach out or explain how I'm feeling, he shuts down. Or worse, he gets so overwhelmed by his own exhaustion that he becomes invisible to me. I look at him and wonder if he even sees *me* anymore, or if he's just waiting for me to stop asking for help so he can finally rest.

And then there's my son. That dynamic is the hardest to reconcile. We used to have those "us against the world" moments where we'd bond over shared struggles. Now, every interaction
It seems like you're both in a state of emotional withdrawal and numbness.

Yeah, that's exactly it. It feels like we're all just sitting in the same room, breathing the same air, but completely disconnected from each other.

With my husband, it's a mutual exhaustion. He's so drained by work and life that he doesn't have the energy to be present emotionally. When I try to talk about how heavy things feel, he either shuts down or gives up on trying to help because he's already at his limit. It's not malice; it's just that both of us are running on empty batteries, and there's no power source left to recharge us together. We've stopped communicating because we don't think we have anything good to say anymore.

And with my son... it's even more confusing. He's 17, an age where you usually expect him to want to grow up, to step out into the world. But right now, he's stuck in this loop of asking for
It's clear that you're both in a state of emotional withdrawal and numbness.
